They built this in orbit, moving at 5 miles per second. 🛰️ Watch 13 years of building in 26 seconds. ⏱️

Piece one, Zarya, launched in November 1998. Unity docked weeks later, then Zvezda in 2000 made it a home: the station has never been empty since November 2000. Then came the giant solar wings, the Destiny lab, a 109 m backbone bolted together on spacewalks, more nodes, Europe's and Japan's labs, and in 2010 a window looking down at Earth.

The twist: all of it was assembled while flying around the planet 16 times a day. 42 assembly flights, about 420,000 kg, nearly a football field long.

Would you live up there for 6 months? Yes or no 👇

yt_title: They Built the Space Station in Orbit at 5 Miles per Second #shorts
yt_description:
ISS assembly: Zarya 20 Nov 1998, Unity 4 Dec 1998, Zvezda 12 Jul 2000 (continuously occupied since Nov 2000), P6 solar arrays 2000, Destiny 2001, truss segments 2000–2009, Harmony 2007, Columbus 2008, Kibō 2008–09, Tranquility + Cupola 2010; US segment completed 2011. 42 assembly flights (37 shuttle, 5 Russian); 109 m end to end; ~420,000 kg; 5 miles per second; 16 orbits a day.

Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assembly_of_the_International_Space_Station · https://www.nasa.gov/international-space-station/space-station-facts-and-figures/
